newsitem.title: USA: Infoseek Q2 loss widens on higher revenues.
newsitem.headline: Infoseek Q2 loss widens on higher revenues.

text.p: Infoseek Corp. said its second quarter loss widened to $11.9 million despite a sharp increase in revenues.
Revenues rose 134 percent on the year and 25 percent on the first quarter to $7.7 million as traffic on its Internet navigation service grew 31 percent from the first quarter.

The loss compares with a net loss of $4.7 million in the second quarter a year ago. Earnings per share were $0.45, on a basis of 26.3 million shares outstanding, compared to $0.52 based on 9.2 million shares a year ago.

The per share loss was three times as deep as the Zacks survey's consensus estimate of $0.15 a share loss for the quarter. According to Zacks, analysts' per-share projection for the full year is a loss of $0.49.

The results were reported after the close. Before the release, Infoseek closed up 1-1/16 at 6-7/16 in active trade of nearly 2.9 million shares, more than 10 times normal daily volume over the past three months.

The company said in a statement Infoseek had delivered an average of approximately eight million page views a day in June and, according to PC Meter's May 1997 report, its navigation site ranks among the top ten sites in reach and overall traffic on the Internet.

Harry Motro, president and CEO of Infoseek, said the company had discontinued non-strategic activities and put into place "infrastructure for aggressive branding efforts" since he joined Infoseek early in the quarter.

Infoseek said sales of its Ultraseek Server software accounted for around six percent of total revenue in the quarter, with Ford Motor Co. and National Aeronautics and Space Administration among its customers.
In April, Infoseek became the search technology provider for CNET Inc's SEARCH.COM service.
